Bishop Robert Barron is America's most prominent Catholic media bishop, founder of a ministry that reaches millions online. With Tucker Carlson, he discusses the reality of demons as the Church teaches it. He also discusses how to fight them with prayer. A third subject is his long project of answering the new atheists on their own rational ground.

Barron's manner is the opposite of the firebrand's: measured, literary, and confident that faith survives argument. Carlson, whose own turn toward spiritual conflict is recent, questions him as a student of the tradition Barron represents. The episode gives listeners the intellectual wing of the current Catholic revival in conversation with its political wing. Preserved at this length, it shows what the two wings share, a belief that the demonic is real and modern, and where their tones part company.
podcast-dannyjones-cIwh6mLQFO0:
Author Annie Jacobsen joins Danny Jones to warn that the Pentagon plans for a doomsday plague. Jacobsen writes books based on deep talks with defense staff. Her work names the plans that sit in files most people never see.

Jacobsen explains how the defense world games out germ attacks and mass death. She walks through the labs, the war games, and the grim math in the plans. Jones asks how close such plans sit to real events. Listeners get a cold look at a dark corner of state planning. The library holds the talk as an archive record of her reporting and claims.
podcast-joerogan-MkqDA9W4Vo0:
Mike Benz returns to the Joe Rogan Experience for episode 2447 with more on the censorship system he calls the blob. Benz, a former State Department official, maps how government and nonprofits steer online speech. Each visit adds new agencies, grants, and programs to his chart.

Benz walks through fresh cases of posts and accounts he says were targeted for political reasons. He argues the system now runs on habit, funding itself year after year. Rogan asks how a new administration could actually dismantle it. The wary and the watchful get the deep state's internet mapped once again, in finer detail.
